reviewers.interpretation_notes: Evaluated against the targets as adopted (the 2023-2026 Carbon Budget report FCS01478 states them explicitly). Community and corporate (City-operations) emissions were kept separate per the brief; corporate status is reported as context only. Latest published inventory found: 2024 community GHG inventory, reported in the Fall 2025 Carbon Budget Update (FCS03160, November 24, 2025). No 2025 inventory or newer City on-track assessment was found as of September 1, 2026.
Interpreted 'on track' as whether the most recent community emissions data aligns with the targets and carbon budget trajectory set out by the City of Edmonton.

I evaluated community emissions, not emissions from City operations. The latest inventory located covers 2024. I treated completed climate actions and per-capita improvement as evidence of progress, but not as proof of trajectory compliance.

round2_positions.interpretation_notes: Position unchanged after cross-review: Contradicted, High confidence. All three reviewers independently reached Contradicted from City-published sources, but agreement is not the basis for my confidence; the basis is the Fall 2025 Carbon Budget Update (FCS03160), which I verified directly in round 1 and which reports the 2024 inventory 3.0 Mt above the City's own trajectory alongside the City's explicit statement that the 2025 target will not be met. Round 2 added two 2026-dated City corroborations from reviewer A (Spring 2026 Budget Highlights; Engaged Edmonton FAQ) that I could only partially verify, so I carry them at moderate strength; the verdict does not depend on them. Community and corporate emissions remain separated per the brief.

Interpreted 'on track' as whether the most recent community emissions data aligns with the targets and carbon budget trajectory set out by the City of Edmonton. In Round 2, I incorporated the 2024 inventory data sourced by other reviewers, which replaces the 2023 data I initially relied on, especially since my original primary URL failed verification.

I evaluated community-wide emissions, not emissions from City operations. Cross-review added a clearer primary source for the adopted targets and evidence of the earlier 2023 miss. Neither changes the decisive evidence: the latest inventory covers 2024, exceeds the required trajectory, and the City's newer Spring 2026 assessment expressly says Edmonton is not on track. Completed initiatives and per-capita improvement show progress but not trajectory compliance. Verdict remains Contradicted independently of the other reviewers' agreement.
